speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. I hear you have progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties; to begin my assessment, have these symptoms been getting worse over time, or did they appear suddenly?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain and Spinal Cord findings indicate multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of Cellulitis is incorrect based on your neurological symptoms; cellulitis is a skin infection and does not cause walking difficulties or speech issues. You mentioned a doctor noted "rigidity in limbs" and "orthostatic hypotension" alongside your tremor and incontinence; were these symptoms present from the very beginning of your illness, or did they develop later?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA).

Your combination of parkinsonism (rigidity, tremor), autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence), and cerebellar signs (gait and speech difficulties) is classic for MSA, not cellulitis. Given your history, I need to confirm the extent of the cerebellar degeneration; are you aware of any intention tremors or problems with balance when standing still?
